header: How I read a vehicle identification number (VIN): "MALBM51BLKM000001" -> world manufacturer MAL (Hyundai Motor India), the maker's own descriptor BM51B, position 9 L (not a check digit: Indian makers use it for their own code), model year K (2019), plant M, serial 000001. Pure; nothing is stored or sent anywhere. The structure is ISO 3779 (the 17 characters) and ISO 3780 (the World Manufacturer Identifier, which SAE International assigns); the letters I, O and Q are never used, so that nothing is mistaken for 1 or 0. Positions 1-3 are the WMI, 4-9 the Vehicle Descriptor Section (VDS), 10-17 the Vehicle Indicator Section (VIS). The check digit of position 9 (a weighted sum modulo 11) is required in North America and is NOT used by Indian makers. What a maker puts in positions 4-8, the plant letter and the month is the maker's own business: my reader says only what the standard fixes, names the manufacturer and plant only where I am sure, and says plainly when a part is the maker's own code. The vehicle's papers (registration certificate, invoice) and the maker are the authority. Indian chassis plates: Hyundai stamps the VIN followed by "*" and a letter for the month of manufacture (MALBM51BLKM000001*L: L = November); I read that suffix and guess nothing else.

symbols.name: VIN_CHAR
doc: The characters of a VIN: digits and capital letters except I, O and Q.

symbols.name: YEAR_CODES
doc: I list the year codes of position 10 in order: A = 1980 (and 2010), ... Y = 2000 (2030), 1 = 2001 (2031) ... 9 = 2009 (2039); I, O, Q, U, Z and 0 are never year codes.

symbols.name: regionOf
symbols.sig: export function regionOf(vin: string): { region: string; country: string | null }
doc: Returns the region (first character) and, where the first two characters fix it, the country.

symbols.name: yearsFor
symbols.sig: export function yearsFor(code: string): number[] | null
doc: Returns the years a position-10 code may stand for: one in each 30-year cycle (null for a letter or digit that is never a year code).

symbols.name: modelYear
symbols.sig: export function modelYear(code: string, nowYear: number): { year: number; other: number } | null
doc: I take the year it most likely is to be the latest of the two that is not later than next year; `other` is the one 30 years earlier (or later).

symbols.name: checkSteps
symbols.sig: export function checkSteps(vin: string): { steps: CheckStep[]; sum: number; remainder: number; digit: string }
symbols.returns: { steps: CheckStep[]; sum: number; remainder: number; digit: string }
doc: Works out the check-digit sum of a 17-character VIN step by step; position 9 has weight 0 because it is the digit being checked.

members.name: prefixed
doc: Set when a word such as "vin" or "chassis number" came before the number.

members.name: core
doc: The characters, upper case, without spaces and hyphens, up to any "*".

members.name: suffix
doc: What followed a "*" (Hyundai's month letter), upper case.

symbols.name: splitVin
doc: Splits what was typed into the number and its extension.

symbols.name: looksLikeVin
doc: Decides whether this line is a VIN that I should read as the person types. I am strict when no word like "vin" is in front: 17 valid characters, letters and digits, and a possible year code at position 10.

members.name: from
doc: 1-based positions

members.name: found
doc: What position 9 holds and what the sum says it would be.

members.name: state
doc: The state of position 9. "valid": a check digit that matches; "mismatch": a digit or X that does not match; "none": a letter, so no check digit.

members.name: warnings
doc: Worries that do not stop me from reading the number (a position-10 code that is never a year).

symbols.name: readVin
symbols.sig: export function readVin(raw: string, nowYear: number = DateTime.now().year): VinReading | VinProblem
doc: Reads what each part of a VIN means, and what follows from it. `nowYear` fixes "next year" for the tests.

behaviours: known numbers get their known check digit: 1HGBH41JXMN109186 is X, 5YJSA1DG9DFP14705 is 9, 1M8GDM9AXKP042788 is X, all ones is 1
the steps are shown: 17 positions, position 9 has weight 0, the sum modulo 11 is the digit (10 is X)
the likely year is the latest one that is not later than next year: K is 2019, V is 2027 in 2026 but 1997 in 2024, 3 is 2003
a Hyundai India number is read part by part: country, manufacturer, descriptor, position 9, year, plant, serial
M with A is India, MAL is Hyundai Motor India
position 9 L is a letter: not a check digit, Indian makers use it for their own code
K is 2019 (or 1989); the plant letter M is Hyundai's Sriperumbudur plant; the descriptor is the maker's own
the facts: 17 characters, India, 2019, check digit not used
the plate may carry Hyundai's month letter after a star: *L is November, the stamped number is 19 characters
the month letters of Hyundai: A January ... H August, J September, K October, L November, M December (no I)
an extension on another maker's number is not guessed
an American number with a right check digit says it is right
a wrong check digit in North America is a probable typing mistake, and says what it should be
outside North America a digit that does not match is not called an error
the wrong length is said: 16 typed, none typed, 11 (before 1981)
I, O and Q are refused with the likely digit: I as 1, O and Q as 0
a character that is not a letter or digit is refused
a year code that is never one gives a warning but the rest is still read
an unknown manufacturer code is said to be unknown, not guessed
spaces, hyphens and lower case are ignored; a word like VIN or chassis number in front is taken off
a line is taken for a VIN, as you type, only when it is one: 17 valid characters, letters and digits, a possible year code; or when it says vin
regions: M is Asia, MA-ME India; 1, 4, 5 United States; J Japan; W Germany; KM South Korea; S UK; Z Italy
the manufacturers of India that are listed are the well-established ones, all MA-ME
the full forms: VIN, WMI, VDS, VIS, the two ISO standards, SAE
the three sections cover positions 1 to 17 without a gap or an overlap
the samples are all readable, and none is the owner's vehicle (serial 000001 or textbook examples)
